utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everybody. Good morning, Mr. Gicevic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would you take the solemn declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please be seated. Yes, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Gicevic.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Would you please state your full name.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Alen Gicevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you testify before the Tribunal in the trials of Dragomir Milosevic and Momcilo Perisic?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And did you give written statements to the Office of the Prosecutor in November 1995 and April 2006?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: On the 16th of February, 2010, did you provide an amalgamated statement which contains relevant parts from your prior testimony and your statements?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I would ask that Exhibit 65 ter 22094 be brought up onto the screen, and in particular the first and the tenth page. Actually, that's enough.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Is that your amalgamated statement?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to review that amalgamated statement recently?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Gicevic, can you confirm that your amalgamated statement accurately reflects your evidence in the past?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Would you provide that same evidence to the Court if questioned on the same matters here today?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the answers would be the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, the following two corrections need to be made to the statement. It's just corrections of references. On page 3, from line [sic] onwards, the photo 65 ter 10191 is referred to, and that's not indicated in any footnote. And in footnote 20, at page 6, the reference should read "65 ter 13143," because the witness was marking the same photo as in footnote 19. And these corrections replace the corrigenda on the final page of the amalgamated statements. Your Honour, I would like to tender this testimony, 65 ter 22094, for admission under Rule 92 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1690, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: With the Court's permission, I would now read a brief summary of the witness's evidence as admitted. During the years 1992 to 1995, Mr. Gicevic was a resident of Sarajevo and was a victim of shelling and sniping. On the 22nd of April, 1992, he was wounded by a shell near his house in the center of Sarajevo, and he received injuries to his leg and his stomach as a result. The apartment in which Mr. Gicevic lived with his parents was damaged twice due to shelling. In addition, the apartment was repeatedly struck by gun-fire. On 3rd March 1995, the first day of Bajram holiday and during a cease-fire, Mr. Gicevic was a passenger in a crowded tram heading towards the center of Sarajevo that came under fire near the Holiday Inn. The witness was shot in the leg and hospitalised as a result of his injury. Another passenger was also struck by a bullet. The area where the tram was shot at was known for sniper fire from Bosnian Serb positions so that anti-sniper barriers had been set up to protect the civilian population. There were no military installations in the immediate area where the tram was hit, nor was there any military activity there that day. The witness concluded that the shots were fired from an area held by Bosnian Serb forces. During the summer of 1995, Mr. Gicevic on several occasions observed unarmed civilians coming under fire on Marsala Tita Street. The firing appeared to come from a white high-rise building situated in Serb-held Grbavica. Your Honours, this concludes the summary. I have just a very few questions to clarify some locations that the witness addressed in his amalgamated statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Gicevic, during your previous testimonies, you were asked to mark quite a number of maps and photos. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I would ask that Exhibit 65 ter 10189 be brought up onto the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And as it is coming up: It is a photo with some markings in red on it. Mr. Gicevic, did you make these markings?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The last times when I gave evidence, I made these markings.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can you tell us what the red markings indicate, starting with this little arrow in the middle of this photo?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: The little arrow marks the place where the tram was hit during this incident.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And the direction of the tram, was it going to the left or the right?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: On this photograph, it was on the right. The tram was moving from the left to the right.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And you also mentioned the front-line in your amalgamated statement. Where would that be?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: It was in the valley of the Miljacka River, and that is the dotted line that goes from left to right.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And the number 2 -- the circle with the number 2, what is this?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I can barely see it here, I mean the numbers. Number 2, as far as I can see, is this tall white building, the skyscraper. Yes, that's it, that's number 2, and I assume that it's the shot that hit the tram -- or, rather, the shots that hit the tram could have come from that skyscraper. And that was a well-known sniper nest.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And the circle -- the circle with the number 3, what does this circle indicate?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: The circle with the number 3 denotes the Metalka building, another building that was well known as being one from which snipers operated.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In your written evidence - and it's at page 7 [Realtime transcript read in error "5"], Your Honour - you describe that just past the place of the incident where the tram was hit, the tram tracks turn to the right side of the street. Do you know since when this curve or bend existed?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, that curve has been there since the last reconstruction, and that was a few years before the Olympic Games that were held in 1984. Since then, there have been no reconstructions of this tram track.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, I request the admission of this exhibit, 65 ter --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P1691.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I would ask that now Exhibit 65 ter 10191 be brought up onto the screen, please, and it is another photo with some markings in blue.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you make these markings in the previous testimony?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What does this blue -- long blue line that you marked with number 6, what does it indicate?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: It was the road that people took from one side of the city to the other. It was called the Salvation Road, the Salvation Route, the Route of Hope, whatever people called it. And from the Jewish cemetery in Grbavica and the territory on the other side of the Miljacka River that was held by the Bosnian Serbs, it was exposed to sniper fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And this dotted line on the right side with number 7 on it, if it is number 7 - I think it's 7 - what is this?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: It may denote the row of containers that protected people from fire. Also, it can be the place where the tram stopped. That would be it.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And you have marked here several circles, circles with "10," "11," and "12." What would that be?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Those were well-known crossroads where civilians were being fired at many times.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I request the admission of this exhibit as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P1692, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, if you could be kind enough to show me the portion where the witness refers to the curve in his statement. You said, In page 5.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Let me just see. No, page 7. Then I had misspoken. It's on page 7, where he describes the -- where he describes the place where the incident occurred and that there was a track -- where he describes where the track was running. It's at line 15 to 18, where he describes the tracks running from the left side to the right side of the street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Page 7 on the hard copy?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, page 7. I misspoke.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Gicevic, were you living in Sarajevo throughout the war?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You described the living conditions in Sarajevo during the period from summer 1992 to the end of 1995 as difficult. Your Honour, that's on page 2. Can you explain what you mean by "difficult"?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I mean in every sense of the word. It was a struggle for bare survival. There was a shortage of food, of electricity. Then when there's no electricity, there's no water either. There were shells, there was sniper fire, gun-fire. Therefore, many glass panes had been broken, and during the winter it was very hard to heat apartments. And above all, there was this uncertainty related to bare survival. There were sudden shellings, gun-fire. It was a struggle for bare survival over three years.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And you described your physical injuries you sustained during the events in your written evidence, and we do not need to repeat that. Your experience during the years 1992 to 1995, did it also have any psychological effect on you during the events and perhaps even afterwards?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: There are physical and psychological effects. I am struggling somehow with the psychological effects and the physical ones also.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And what do you mean by "psychological effects"?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, psychologically, if there are 1.000 days of such uncertainty, any normal person would have to be affected. We are trying to find ways of forgetting all of that, but as a physician from Sarajevo said once, the brain may have forgotten, but the body still recalls.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, this concludes the examination-in-chief. I would now request the three remaining associated exhibits referred to in the amalgamated statement be admitted. It would be 10188, 10439 and 13143.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. With respect to 10439, which is a police report of 24 pages, I note that the witness did say that he reviewed it, and this is on page 9 in his statement, and he -- the facts set out in the file agree with his recollection of the incident. But I don't think it's a good practice to admit an entire police report through a person who's not a police officer, because it contains many things besides his own statement - conclusions, forensic examination - and I don't think it's proper -- I think it deprives us of confrontation rights to admit a police report through a witness who simply says it agrees with his recollection of the incident. So we would be objecting, although we note that the police officers involved will be coming to testify, and perhaps it could more properly be admitted when they testify. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I have only added this document here because it is mentioned in the amalgamated statement, and it was actually discussed extensively with this witness in the earlier testimony. But as the police officer is, indeed, coming as the next witness, I would not insist on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Well, that being the case, then we'll -- can I take it that you are withdrawing that exhibit in relation to this witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Then there being no objection, those two exhibits will be admitted. Shall we give them the number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. 65 ter 10188 will be Exhibit P1693, and 65 ter 13143 will be Exhibit P1694.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. That's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Excellency. Good morning to all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Gicevic.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you to tell us what kind of education you've had.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I have a university degree in Economics.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Before that?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Before that, I completed the high school called Druga Gimnazija in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And in the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, you worked as a nurse, right, a medical technician, as we say?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I worked as an ambulance driver and, when necessary, as medical staff as well. That was my VS in the JNA, because I did my military service in Mostar, and that's where I was an ambulance driver as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Since we are speaking the same language, could I ask you to pause between question and answer so it would be possible for the interpreters to interpret what we are saying. In the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, you were, between August 1992 to July 1994; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: From April 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says here "from August," so that's wrong. All right. So from April 1992 until July 1994. In which unit?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: First, I was in the Territorial Defence, and after that I was in the Command of the Medical Corps of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, from August 1992, in the 101st Brigade.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 07078 [as interpreted]. Could we have page 1 of that document, please. 07048.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This has been admitted as Exhibit P1058.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where was your brigade deployed?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: From August 1992, it was on Hrasno Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you were the driver for that brigade?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now zoom in on this map, where it says the "101st Brigade." A bit more. A bit more, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark, with that pen, the area of responsibility of the 101st Brigade, and the lines that it covers, and where you did your driving.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you, it is very hard to see anything on this map. I can hardly mark anything. I can just describe the line of separation for you, the one that was covered by the brigade. It's very hard for me to see anything here. I wonder who could conceivably see anything on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you discern the airport, Dobrinja, Alipasino Polje, Grbavica, Hrasno Brdo, when you see these markings for different staffs?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I'm saying, once again, I'm very familiar with maps, but I cannot see anything here, Alipasino, nothing, not with this kind of zoom-in.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we zoom out, then, so it's easier for Mr. Gicevic to read this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gicevic, do you see here where it says the "101st Brigade"? Can you discern "Hrasno Brdo," "Grbavica," et cetera?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I see where it says the "101st Brigade," but the rest is very unclear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see these little flags where the staffs are marked of the battalions and companies of the 101st Brigade? Is that Hrasno Brdo?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I am telling you that I cannot say whether it's Hrasno Brdo or not. I assume it is, as long as that is there.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown the paper part of this map that might help him mark it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I wonder, in the meantime, if Mr. Reid could find a map of better quality than this one.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If necessary, we even have a magnifying-glass.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not about magnifying-glasses, it's about the clearness of this map. I don't see who could find his way on this map. You can just read the names of brigades here, nothing else. But I'll try to answer your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please try to use a blue marker, for instance, to mark the area of responsibility of your brigade? And that is the area where you drove that ambulance; right?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Can he be given blue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]. But I'm telling you again that I'm doing this more by intuition rather than relying on the markings on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you see the city of Sarajevo in this map? The both of us know it very well, and we know all the settlements that constitute the city, and do you see the separation line between the HQs of the 101st Brigade and the respective battalions and companies? Can you please -- you have drawn the front-line going through Mojmilo. Can you indicate, where does it link up with the 115th?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Somewhere in the area of the Grbavica Stadium.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And which was the neighbouring unit on the right flank?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: That was the Dobrinja Brigade until they merged sometime in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you then mark, in depth, the area of responsibility of 101st Brigade? You can see these flags going all the way to Dobrinjska Street.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I really don't see how you can see the Dobrinjska Street here. All I can see here is the city and the separation line, and I really congratulate you on being able to find the streets here.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, as much as you can, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I think why do we not use a different map. The witness obviously cannot precisely do what Mr. Karadzic asked him to do. I mean, we have always used so far this map [indicates], and I don't know whether this is an option. I don't know whether this is -- what is supposed to be shown on there.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that we can do that, but this map shows very dense distribution of HQs of the 101st Brigade in the area of Hrasno Brdo all the way to Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This map has been already admitted, and we can rely -- you can rely on this map later on, so why don't we use another map which the witness can easily recognise, having heard from him that --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is it necessary for him to make any markings on this map?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: He says he's not able to mark anything on this map.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we please then use the map that has been kindly offered by Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's 65 ter 09390C.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And what page?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, it's actually the whole map at the moment. I'm not sure which page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, it may be 10 or 14. It's a little bit unclear. Sheet 10 or 14.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, 10. 14 - this is Dobrinja, where the Dobrinja Brigade was. No, this is not 10. This is 8. We need 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gicevic, is it now easier for you to mark the area of responsibility of the forward and -- of the area of responsibility of the 101st Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Please give me time to find my bearings. It is much easier now. Well, there is a separation line here [indicates], more or less. Do I need to mark it on this map?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, we can see the separation line, but can you please mark the linking point with the 115th, and what was the in-depth area of responsibility of the 101st?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know you can ask me to make such markings. I'm not a military expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you worked as a driver.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I drove from the annex to the hospital. I didn't do my driving along the whole line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was Alipasino Polje within the area of responsibility of the 101st Brigade, the Alipasino Polje neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: That is an urban city zone. I don't know how it can be within the responsibility of 101st Brigade's. In other words, troops were deployed along the lines. They were not in the town, unless they went back into town.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you trying to say that the area of responsibility is only marked by a line, that there is no in-depth to it?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I told you I am no military expert. The area of responsibility was above the stadium, all the way to Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have this map on the ELMO. That's 1D255. [In English] May I ask you to enlarge this portion, this portion, this portion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you understand, Mr. Gicevic, now what I'm referring to? You see the front end and you see the area of responsibility. Did you do your driving along this area marked by these hooks?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I already told you I drove from Vrbovska Street to the barracks and then to the State and City Hospital in Kosevo. I didn't drive along the line. I only went in-depth to the barracks and from the barracks to the hospitals.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That was only one route?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Every battalion and every company had their own medical team, and they didn't overlap in their responsibilities. That is what happens in every army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you trying to tell me that you were not at the level of the brigade, but rather at the level of company?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I was at the level of the brigade. But whenever necessary, I went to the battalion HQ on Vrbovska Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you show Vrbovska Street on the ELMO, where the HQ of the battalion was?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly. It runs parallel with Zagorska Street. It's about 200 metres below the line of separation. But just give me a moment to find my bearings. Nevertheless, I think it is impossible to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, having heard the answer from the witness, I would advise you to move on to another topic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: He has come to testify about the F-16 incidents and other shelling incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But I am interested, Mr. Gicevic, how come that you were wounded on Nemanjina Street while you were walking, and then through the zone of the 101st and 115th Brigades you managed to get through unscathed?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know -- you're really insulting my dignity and the evidence that I gave you. I don't know what you expect me to answer to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please do not feel insulted. That's the last thing on my mind. Do you believe that the fact that you drove the ambulance kept you safe from being injured for two years during the war, without happening to you -- anything happening to you whatsoever, but then as a pedestrian you were wounded on Nemanjina Street?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I think that you would be happy if I had been wounded five times as a civilian and two times as a soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gicevic, I just wanted to say that you were safe in the ambulance which you drove within the war zone for two years.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know how it occurred to you at all that I was safe in an ambulance. How can anyone be safe in an ambulance?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was your ambulance ever hit? Were you wounded in your vehicle?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't, luckily.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You say "luckily," but I am saying that this was a decision by the Serbian Army not to shoot at ambulances, and I don't know --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please pause between questions and answers, and slow down. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Gicevic. Because both of you are overlapping in questions and answers while they were interpreted, interpreters couldn't follow your answers. If you could repeat your last answer, Mr. Gicevic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In spite of all the misfortune, I was lucky not to be hit in the ambulance. However, others were not as lucky as I was. A large number of ambulances and people who worked in the Medical Corps, such as doctors and technicians, lost their lives. And you know very well that there were quite a few of such incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gicevic, there is not such an incident in any of the counts in my indictment. Let's move on. You said that you knew - that's in line 19 - that hundreds of people were wounded or killed by shelling and sniping. Which kind of massive incidents are you aware of taking place in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I know the incident of the queue for bread. I know that when children gathered in a playground, happy that they can play some football, I know that people were waiting in queues for water, people were killed and injured at junctions, and that proves why about 10.000 people were killed about three -- during the period of three years.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gicevic, please do not feel that I am trying to attack you. We are just trying to clarify your statement so that we do not have general assertions. Which specific incident are you aware of, as you said on page 2, line 19?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Let me just mention a few of them. The bread queue on the Vase Miskin Street, the two shelling incidents at Markale, the incident that happened near to the brewery in the old town, where people waiting for water were hit, the incident when children and their teacher, Fatima Bunic, were killed on the school playground, where seven or nine or eleven children were killed while playing football during the calm period. So this is a whole mass of people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, I am interested in what you say, this mass and huge number of cases. Do they really exist or is that just a figure of speech of yours?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: From the Vrbanja Bridge towards the new part of the town, you know exactly how many such cases happened at the intersections. Maybe not as many people were killed. And there was an incident in Alipasino Polje, and I know that you are aware of these incidents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Now you may ask.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On page 2, line 25 of your statement, you say that all the intersections along the main street in Sarajevo were notoriously known as sniping targets. These intersections were in Novo Sarajevo, Centar, and Stari Grad municipalities. Can you name these intersections that you would qualify as Sniper Alley? But please be precise in doing so, where exactly these sniping incidents took place.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Of course, I can do that. The intersection under the Hrasno Brdo, Cengic Vila. Then the next one is close to the power electricity company. Then the Pofalici intersection. Then the intersection between the National Museum and Museum of Revolution. Then the one between the Faculty of Philosophy and the National Museum. Then the one between the Executive Council and Philosophy Faculty. Then on the old and new Skenderija Bridge. Near the post office. Near the Skenderi [as interpreted] Mosque. And in all other minor intersections close to the separation line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now this has prompted me to ask you to mark on the map who was killed on the Skenderija Most Bridge.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Are you really expecting me that I have a book from which I can read you the names of the casualties? I, myself, witnessed the shootings taking place at these locations, and don't force me to doubt my own memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, I have to do that anyway, Ms. Gicevic. Can you tell us which locations were targeted in Stari Grad by snipers?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I didn't move around Stari Grad as much as that. All I am telling you is what I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that your memory was somewhat better than it is now?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know what you are alluding to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Generally speaking, did you have a better memory in recollecting these events than you do now?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you trying to say that you are talking about the incidents that you eye-witnessed?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I wasn't present during the incidents. I did see some of them, but the majority of them I didn't see, myself. I don't know how you expect me to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In lines 17 and 18, you say that you were present, and then you go on to say that wherever you were in-situ, you see many incidents. Can you tell us specifically which sniper incidents you witnessed?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Of course I can. I was working in the building across Alipasina Mosque, and there was a container that was protecting Alipasina Street from south, from the direction of the Jewish cemetery. However, in 1995, when I was working there, I noticed that vehicles came under fire from the white high-rise building in Grbavica. I even witnessed an incident when UNPROFOR troops turned their transporter and their guns towards Grbavica. So all in all, there were quite a few incidents of that nature.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please now have P9169 [as interpreted] that has been admitted into evidence earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think you have that number wrong.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: P9161.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. 1691?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: ... 91, recently admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gicevic, can you see the Unis building, Unioninvest, that building?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you mark it with a blue marker? So what would be the next number now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you wait a minute.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go back to the east a bit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Under whose control was the Unis building, Mr. Gicevic?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: The Vrbanja Bridge was the bridge of separation, and you controlled that building, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you look a bit towards the west. Do you see two red buildings? First, you see a red facade, and behind it, another red building to the west of number 5.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: You mean on the right, down here [indicates]?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: To the left from the number 5, horizontally.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: There are many buildings with red roofs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Red facade.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Red facade. To tell you the truth, I cannot see. I just see Metalka. That's red.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Behind Metalka, do you see a red facade to one side? [In English] May I ask you to show to Mr. Gicevic another photo on the same bench, but just to help him orient. [Interpretation] Do you see those two red buildings? You can see them less in this photograph, but on the other one, you can see them better.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I see one red building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And behind it, there's another one.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I really cannot see another red building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you put a circle around the one that you do see.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. The one in front of it is also red, so could you please place number 6 there.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who controlled that building, Mr. Gicevic?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, you did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you now mark the Executive Council building?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The Assembly building?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The building of the Faculty of Philosophy?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The museum building? The entire complex.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That's right. Who controlled those buildings, Mr. Gicevic?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: These buildings, 7, 8, 9 and 10, were under the control of the Army of BH.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, in your early statement from 1995, you said that the tram had been hit as soon as you passed by the Assembly building. Can you now mark that particular spot where the tram had been hit, as you had stated then. Could you mark it with a little asterisk.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand what it is that I'm supposed to mark.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: According to your first statement, where was the tram hit?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Before the Assembly, that's what I stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please put the date there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you like to ask the witness to mark further on this map?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted the witness to mark on this photograph the spot where the tram had been hit, according to his first statement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: According to my first statement, the tram was hit before the Assembly, and I can mark it for you now. [Marks]. I marked it with a little cross.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's not what your first statement says. Can this be admitted, once the date is put on this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Gicevic, can you kindly put the date of today - which is the 11th of October, 2010 - and your signature.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. That will do. In the future, if you're going to mark -- you're going to put the date, put it in the right bottom so that we can see easily. We can -- yes, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I'm just wondering about one thing. The accused put to the witness that in the previous statement he would have said something different, but he didn't really put this statement to the witness so that he can check, and he didn't really give the line or an indication where it is, but I think that would have been correct.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I will follow this well-intentioned suggestion. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D725, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gicevic, now I would like to remind you -- actually, can we call up 65 ter 22089. I believe that it exists in both versions. 22089, that's the 65 ter number. This is your statement dated the 15th of November, 1995; right?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the third paragraph, it says: "The tram passed the building of the Executive Council and was arriving at the level of an anti-sniping barricade formed by two rows of containers." Is that what you stated?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have D725.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The tram was moving from Cengic Vila towards Bascarsija; right?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: From the west to the east; right?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In accordance with this statement of yours, that namely the tram passed the Executive Council building and was getting close to -- can you mark now where that anti-sniper barricade was? You said a few moments ago that it was at Marin Dvor; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Wait. Can you change the colour into black.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The anti-sniper barricades were from the corner at Marsal Tito Barracks all the way up to the old tobacco factory, so it wasn't one particular spot. The entire tram stop had been covered with anti-sniper barricades.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you mark the tram stop at Marin Dvor, towards Bascarsija?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, at Marin Dvor [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you mark it with number 11, please.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, you say in this statement that before the tram was hit, the tram had passed the Executive Council building and that it was hit then; right?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: That's not what I said. I just said that it stopped at the tram stop at Marin Dvor. And of course it has to pass by the Executive Council building. It cannot get off the tram tracks, can it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What is written here is different, but let us move on. Let us see what is written here. Can you mark the spot where the tram stopped, to the best of your belief, after it had been hit?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: That is what I marked with the number 11; that is to say, behind the old tobacco factory, at the stop there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that if we look at the direction in which the tram was moving, you were facing Vraca and the Jewish cemetery, and you could see that from where you were standing.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I was standing on the right-hand side, and I could see the south.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says here: "I was standing on the left-hand side and was facing Vraca and the Jewish cemetery."

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I was standing on the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How tall are you, Mr. Gicevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How high are the windows on the tram?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. First of all, you consider me to be a military expert, and now what? I don't know, two, two and a half metres, whatever. You are really putting some very illogical questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If you're standing there, you can only see the road, asphalt, when you're standing on the tram. If you were sitting on the tram, then that would have been plausible, but you were standing there with your height of 173 centimetres, and you say that you could see Vraca and the Jewish cemetery?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: To put it mildly, you are saying something that has nothing to do with reality. What kind of a tram would that be that wouldn't have any kind of view even when you're standing? That's the way it is in Sarajevo, in The Hague, anywhere in the world.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you still stand by that? As you were standing on the right by the wall, you could see the Jewish cemetery and Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: With 100 per cent certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. From where could have that bullet come; from the Jewish cemetery?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: You keep saying "Jewish cemetery." When I say "Grbavica," "Jewish cemetery," I meant the general direction. I don't mean a particular grave in the Jewish cemetery. I was talking about the general direction. I'm really not that familiar with the Jewish cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that on the eastern wall of the Jewish cemetery, there were the Muslims, and on the western side, there were the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: No. It was the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina that had Muslims, Serbs and Croats, all of them, and on the right-hand side were Serbs only. So that side was held by the Army of Republika Srpska. That is to say that in the cemetery there were no troops of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, the Army of Republika Srpska wasn't in the cemetery, either, but on its western wall; right?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: That's not right. You were in there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In this statement -- or, actually, can we admit this, this picture with the number 11 that we need?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you put your signature and date again, kindly, at the bottom of this picture.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll admit it as D726.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Further on, you say, Mr. Gicevic, that you heard glass breaking; right?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I do not remember having said that at all.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Once again, can we have 65 ter 22089.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the meantime, just briefly, let us deal with this issue of the Chetniks. Do you believe that those Serbs who wanted the Republika Srpska are Chetniks?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Not at all. By "Chetniks," I mean the worst part of the Serb people. Let me be very specific and clear and precise on this. I'm not saying that Serbs and Chetniks are one-and-the-same thing. Serbs are an honourable and honest people, and Chetniks are scum.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You heard a gun-shot, screams, and glass that was breaking. It is towards the middle. Can we have it in English as well. That's where it starts in English: "Suddenly I felt pain in my leg." Here it says that you felt pain in your leg, heard the sound of broken glass, and a shot as well as screams. Did the bullet enter through the window or through metal sheets?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure. That is where my memory is unclear after all this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The next sentence: "I'm not sure, but I think I heard two or three shots. According to the sounds I heard, I'm sure that the shots came from the direction of the Jewish cemetery." So you heard the shots. You did not refer to the tram being hit. You felt pain in your leg, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: The situation was rather chaotic. It wasn't filmed. It's not on camera so that I can analyse it now. I said I heard two or three shots. Were they shots, were they sounds, was it a bullet hitting a window, was it a gun-shot hitting metal? I cannot say. At any rate, I was standing on the tram, and it's only natural to expect that the bullet had come from the right-hand side. It is only logical that it cannot come from the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Why can it not come from the left-hand side?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Because it follows a straight line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And if the Muslims fired?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know where you get that idea, that the Muslims could have fired, when UNPROFOR soldiers were staying there. If you think that a Muslim bullet can go through an UNPROFOR APC and by UNPROFOR soldiers, then you are very wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's move on, Mr. Gicevic. How could you be sure that the gun-shot had come from the direction of the Jewish cemetery? That's that sentence there.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I'm telling you again, I mentioned the Jewish cemetery and Grbavica when I was describing the general direction. I never said that it came exactly from that location. I was talking about the direction and orientation. I said that I thought that the bullet had come from the direction of Grbavica and the Jewish cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please do not feel harassed or attacked. I just want to be precise. You say here that according to the sounds that you heard, you said that you were sure that the shot had come from the Jewish cemetery. I'm not attacking you. If you were sure, as you say you were, based on what were you sure? Can we now modify this and say that you were not quite sure that it had come from the Jewish cemetery?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: The only correction that could be made is that it came from the direction of Grbavica and the Jewish cemetery, as I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: A bullet cannot come from two directions.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what you're talking about. When you talk about direction, which is east-west, we're not talking about grid references. So if you insist that it came from the south, we can discuss that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Excellent. But if we leave it as it is, I'm not sure that you were so sure that the shot came from the Jewish cemetery.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. The interpreters were not able to hear your last answer, Mr. Gicevic. Could you repeat it, kindly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am positive that the bullet came from the south, where the Jewish cemetery and Grbavica are located, and therefore I concluded that it had come from that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, can I please ask you to read the sentence that starts: "According to the sounds ..." somewhere in the middle of the sheet.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: "According to the sounds that I heard, I am sure that fire came from the direction of the Jewish cemetery."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, talking about the south, between the tram, wherever it is hit, and the Jewish cemetery or, rather, Grbavica, were there any other positions?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know which particular positions you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Military positions. Were there any troops deployed in the area between the tram and Grbavica, someone else?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: No, there weren't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: There was no line held by the Muslims on the Miljacka River?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: You know very well that not a fly could survive from sniper fire, let alone troops.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, as you said, did not hold the building of the Executive Council, the Assembly, the museum, the faculty, et cetera. It was -- these were not under their control; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: As far as I knew, those were merely observation posts manned by a few soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So why didn't the Serbs capture these positions and connect it with the Marsal Tito Barracks?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Because they tried this several times and were slapped on the knuckles.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: By whom?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: These are just the insinuations that you are making.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Later on, you worked on Marsal Tito number 8?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Number 5, although I am not sure about the number. It's the building across the mosque and where the Forestry Administration was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Which building is adjacent to this building westwards?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Westwards, it is surrounded by the Sutjeska Radnik Cinemas, the Institute for Public Health, Alipasina mosque. That's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: To the west, behind that building, was there an old military hospital that was converted into a military depot?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: That was a state hospital, and I am not familiar with that notion of a military depot. I know that for sure because both my father and my sister used to work there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. So you don't know that next to the Forestry building there was a large yard, and the big building of the old military hospital that had been converted into a military depot a long time ago, and from the northern part is the Kranjcevica Street; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, you know very well that the old military hospital was so much destroyed that it collapsed by itself, and I really cannot believe what you are insinuating, that some weapons and other things were kept there. It would have been put in a much more secure building, not the building that collapsed by itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: To the west of the Forestry building, was there a complex of the old military hospital? You don't have to say that it was a military depot.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I confirm that behind the Forestry building there was an old military hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this military hospital across the intersection between Vrazovo and Tito Vraz?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You say here that you were hit in the right thigh, and that you were bleeding, and that you -- actually, your girlfriend helped you to tie it up with a scarf; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where were you exactly hit?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Ten or five or six centimetres above the knee.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How far from the ground is that?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps 50 or 60 centimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It would be very important to us if we knew the exact figure.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, if you wish, I can stand up and have you measure it, if you think that is necessary.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have this 1995 statement admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How did you leave the incident place?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: When the tram stopped near the old tobacco factory, my girlfriend and I went to Zagreb Hotel, and then from there we went to the State Hospital which is some 200 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In some statements, Mr. Gicevic, you said that you walked to the hospital; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I said that -- this memory is a little bit blurred, and I cannot be quite sure whether I walked or whether I took a taxi. It's not a long distance from the place where I was to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have this admitted into evidence, and then we can move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. His statement of 15th November 1995 will be admitted as Exhibit D727. And I note the time. How much longer do you have with this witness, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would need considerably more than envisaged by the Trial Chamber, because there is quite a few contradictions, so it's a complete [indiscernible].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll take the break now, and you will have half an hour after the break, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By your leave, this is far from sufficient for this single incident. Mr. Gicevic mentioned so many things that if they are entered into the record, I cannot consider to have a defence case. These things need to be refuted, or we have to discard his statement in its entirety, or I should be allowed to cross-examine him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You should have prioritized your questions. You were given notice that you would have one hour and a half with this witness, and you spent a lot of time asking unhelpful questions as to the location of 101st Brigade or those things. Plan your remaining of your cross-examination so that you can finish in half an hour after the break, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we please have in e-court 65 ter 21215. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gicevic, can I ask you to tell us if you recognise this photograph.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please draw a line, by using an electronic pen, along the then Marsala Tita Street along which the tram service runs.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I can show you where the tram runs, but this is the end of Marsala Tita Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But can you show us the section between Marin Dvor --

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: -- and the intersection? Thank you. Can you put number 1 somewhere on the line?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please now draw a line that runs along the Vranje Rackog Street.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: That's the street that you're looking for, if I'm not mistaken [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you think that this is the street and the intersection that firing took place?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Among others, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please put number 2.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you put the number 3 where these two lines join together.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you now see the so-called Metalka building?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I think that the Metalka building is more to the west.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I am not sure. There was an advertisement on one of those buildings. It's either of the two. Both of them are called "Metalka," so I'm not sure whether it's the one on the right or the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you encircle Unioninvest building and the two red buildings that you had marked previously.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the red one with number 6.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that the Franje Rackog Street is situated between the museum and the faculty, the parallel street?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question? I didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do we agree that the Franje Rackog Street is situated between the museum and the faculty? Can you mark the museum with number 7 and the faculty with number 8.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Museum, number 7 [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the Faculty of Philosophy, number 8, please.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, I made a mistake. The Franje Rackog Street is to the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you mark it now correctly?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So that would be number 9, Franje Rackog Street?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree, then, that the Metalka is where these two streets join or, rather, in the direction of Franje Rackog Street?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I'm telling you again, I don't remember where the advertisement was placed on top of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this street used to be called Djure Danicica, and it's now called Kosta Hermana Street?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know how it was called before or how is it called now, but that's the one that I marked with number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please put a date in the corner of this photo - within the photo, not outside of the frame - and sign it.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Although the participants know very well, but could you please mark Holiday Inn with number 10 and the Executive Council building with number 11.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the Assembly number 12.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Unis high-rise buildings, number 13.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we please admit this map -- correction, this photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D728, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have D727 in e-court. That's the statement. D727, that's your 1995 statement. Can we also have the Serbian version, please. Thank you. Can we now have page 2, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please look where it says: "The confrontation line was 200 metres. "All the tram was full. All the seats were occupied." And then we have the next sentence, which starts with: "I have put a red cross ..."

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: "I have put a red cross on a map that I have signed in order to pin-point the spot where the event happened. The arrow shows the direction of the tram."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 22091, please. 65 ter 22091. Can we please enlarge the section around Marin Dvor and the red markings. Can we please enlarge it to a little bit more.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you put these markings?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I suppose so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that it says here "Djure Danicica Street" between the faculty and the Parliament and the Government building?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't see this inscription anywhere, but if you say so, I have no reason not to believe you. Oh, yes, I can see it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please now draw a line from Unioninvest and red buildings along the middle part of Djure Danicica Street, and please use the blue pen.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please mark on the map the street Franje Rackog Street, number 87.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And can you put a circle around the Executive Council now, and could you put a number there, let's say number 3.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Parliament, 4?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Vrbanja Bridge?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The Unioninvest building, 6?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: 1 Djure Danicica Street; number 2, Rackog.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does this map correspond to your statement of 1995?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I see that it lacks in precision a bit. I guess that when I drew that asterisk -- I mean, if I were to draw it now, I would have put it to the left a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And who had made that suggestion to you?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: How do you get this idea that someone gave a suggestion to me? No one did. I thought it would be necessary -- I mean, I just wanted to show the place where the incident took place, roughly. I was not measuring it in metres. If I were to be doing it now, I would pay attention to every little metre or centimetre, in terms of where I placed the asterisk.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let me just read this: "I used a red cross to mark on the map the spot where the event happened." So could we have today's date and your initials on this document now.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can it be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you continue from that red asterisk, you marked another asterisk in blue or something like that. What does it refer to, Mr. Gicevic, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't see a blue asterisk. Ah-hah, that is Marsala Tita Street, where I worked. And from this white skyscraper, there was sniper fire. Then this is the intersection of these streets.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you put a circle now in red or blue - it's one-and-the-same thing - around the building where you worked and the intersection of these two streets, Titova and Vrazova?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Now, what number would that be? 7, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I believe it's 7.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can it be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D729, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What is 8?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: The intersection, the BH Suma, the Cinemas of Sutjeska near the Hygiene Institute.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Radava?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Radava is the next street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you put a line along Vrazova?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: It's right below this asterisk. As far as I can see, it should be here [marks]. Yes, it should be 369.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Do we need to place the date here again, and should it be signed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do we need this? Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We cannot hear the speaker. Could all other microphones please be switched off. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Has this been recorded, the circles around Suma and the rest? Actually, those previous markings, Djure Danicica and Rackog, that previous map with the markings, the previous map with the previous markings?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think we can safely move on. Shall we keep this one? Is it necessary? Then can you take a look at the previous one which we just saved.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excellent. If it's been admitted, then it's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gicevic, how many gun-shots did you hear?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I heard two or three sounds. Now, was it a gun-shot, was it impact on metal or glass or my leg, or was it the sound of a bullet being fired? I don't know, but I heard two or three sounds.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was the time that elapsed between them?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: It's hundredths of a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Like a burst of gun-fire?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Not like a burst of gun-fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But hundredths of a second, that means it could have been at least 30 and 1 second [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: All right, then tenths of a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you help us with this now: How far up from the floor is your wound?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I told you a moment ago; 50 centimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Above the knee?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: It's right by the knee, itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It was a bullet fragment that hit you; right?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How did that happen if the bullet had not hit another obstacle before that?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: You're asking me way too much. I'm not a doctor or a forensic expert.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 15525, could we have that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And while we're waiting: Mr. Gicevic, was there any fighting on that day in that area?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, the two or three days before Bajram, it was peaceful, or relatively peaceful, rather.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting for the document: How many wounded or killed persons did you transport? Did you transport the wounded and the killed of the 101st Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Only the wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How many?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Thirty to forty.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Per day?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: No. The first half year, I carried the wounded, and then for about a year, I worked as a driver. So during that period, it was perhaps 20 or 30 or 60. I mean, I really can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So 60 over a period of 360 days?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I wasn't always at the front-line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to draw your attention to the 3rd of March, 1995. This is a regular combat report to the president of Republika Srpska and the corps commanders. It's a report sent by the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska. Could we have page 2. Have a look at what it says, paragraph 4: "The enemy ...," and then it's the Majevica front -- actually, no, sorry, 3, paragraph 3: "The Sarajevo Romanija Corps. The enemy opened fire from rifle grenades in the area of Vrbanja bridge ..." And so on and so forth: "They opened fire from PATs, PAMs. Our forces were unaffected." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. That's just what I wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI 730, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How many wounded were there in this tram incident, Mr. Gicevic?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Two or three.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You were wounded in the leg. Somebody who was sitting was hit in the abdomen; right?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you give your seat to that person?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
