utterances.text: Do you know that a bullet was taken out of that man's abdomen that was 7.62 millimetres?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. You live in Dzidzikovac Street number 8; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the map, 9390C, and then section 7. This is not 7. Can we have 7? This is 5. Yes, this is it. Can you zoom in on the lower central part. Precisely, over there. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gicevic, can you mark Dzidzikovac Street for us and the place where your apartment was?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So is this Dzidzikovac and Sutjeska merging into one?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And what is the building below number 1?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: That is Dom Milicija, the police building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you put a circle around Dom Milicija and mark it with number 2.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you draw a line along Cekalusa, which used to be Nemanjina?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Further on, towards Bolnicka, could you draw a line there and then mark the School of Dentistry, the Secondary School of Dentistry, the University School of Dentistry, and so on.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So it's the Secondary School of Dentistry, and opposite it is the university building of the School of Dentistry?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that there were commands and bunkers there and artillery pieces?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know what kind of bunkers you're talking about in the center of town. Now, whether there was some commands there, that is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you just put a little cross there, "X1," where you were wounded by a shell in Cekalusa?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gicevic, can you explain to us now from which position somebody could have targeted your apartment using a sniper?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: From Grbavica and artillery pieces could have targeted it from Trebevic. So this is the direction of artillery fire [marks], and this is the direction -- I didn't say of sniper fire. I said rifle fire and larger calibres as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So then could you put number 6 there for artillery fire, as you had put it.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the one towards Grbavica -- well, how far is it from the Serb positions in Grbavica to your apartment? How big is the distance?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: It's a pretty big distance, but don't tell me that a PAM cannot deal with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was your apartment hit with a PAM?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: It wasn't hit by a PAM, but there is nothing that did not hit it; tank shells, PAMs, PATs, rifle fire. We had an entire collection of souvenirs that we just threw away.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gicevic, you said that your apartment had been hit by sniper fire from Serb positions. Can you tell us from which Serb positions your apartment was hit, within what range?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I said "fire."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you please put the date and your initials on this map.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While the map is still there, could you please mark Bjelave Street right there?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know what was in Dom Milicija, the police building?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was a police building and there were some police units there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know where the training centre was at Bjelave?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I cannot say where the training centre was at Bjelave.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now let me remind you of your statement that you gave on the 21st of April, 2006. This is what you said: "Apart from shelling, our apartment had been hit 10 or 15 times by sniper fire."

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: When I said "sniper," I meant "ammunition." I did not say that somebody targeted me while I was standing at the window. After all, the building is still scarred, so if you come there, you can check for yourself, and you will see that there are hundreds and hundreds of potholes on these buildings that were hit in this way.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll go back to this statement where it says it was sniper fire. Thank you. So can we have this admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This map marked by the witness will be admitted as Exhibit D731.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gicevic, on this map scale it seems that from Grbavica to your apartment, there is more two kilometres.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, roughly. Perhaps a bit less.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have something else now? You worked in the Forestry building. Can we now have 1D2542.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please mark here the building where you worked, the Institute of Hygiene, the mosque, and the entry point to Vrazova Street?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just hold it a minute.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I worked on the ground floor of this building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you kindly wait until the usher helps you right now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]. So this is the building where I worked [marks]. This is the Institute of Hygiene.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Number 2, you worked on the ground floor?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. [Marks]. Number 3 is the Hygiene Institute, and then we have the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We are in a haste because we are pressed for time. So number 1 is the building where you worked, number 2 is the Institute of Hygiene, 3 is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. 3 should be the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please now mark on the pavement, or even on the road itself, where the detour into Vrazova Street is?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And can you mark the building where we have the sign "Vrazova," mark the wall viewed from Titova Street?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And could you also put the date and your initials.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have this admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Exhibit D732. Mr. Karadzic, you will have five minutes to conclude.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, that would mean that I wouldn't have been finished, if you don't extend it. We are trying to be as quick as possible.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the accused please repeat the document number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you repeat the number?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D02541.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise this intersection?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It's the same one that we looked a minute ago, only viewed from a different angle.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On this red building, viewed from Titova Street, can you put number 1, which you previously marked with number 5? Now you will get some assistance.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you draw a line along the Vrazova Street so that we can know it's Vrazova Street? Number 2.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now the central line along Titova Street.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Gicevic, in the background, on the horizon, can you indicate a line that indicates the road via Trebevic [marks].

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, that could be it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That's right. Do you agree that the name of this hill is Vranjaca?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, above Vranjaca [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Vranjaca is below this line.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know where the separation line was in this location? Or, more precisely, can you use a red pen and mark it?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I cannot find my bearings here. This resolution is too small and I honestly cannot see. I know that the VRS was up there [marks] where this line on Zlatiste goes on, but I cannot be more precise as to where the separation line was. But, anyway, below these pine trees.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you now draw a line starting a little below the blue line and the intersection, itself?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know what you are talking about. I never said that shots came here. I said that the shots came from the white high-rise building on Titova Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm only asking you to draw a straight line from the separation line all the way to the intersection.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know which separation line or point you referred to. Which one would you like?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the middle, all the way to the intersection.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And more to the east?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, that's what you told me to mark.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, then, put another line from the far east.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That's the middle. Can you do it from the far eastern part?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: No, I cannot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Because I think these were the VRS positions to the left of the Jewish cemetery, if that is what you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we see the Jewish cemetery here?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can see, one cannot see it. If we can enlarge it, but at the moment I cannot see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you now put the letter S in this photograph above the Serb-controlled territory.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gicevic, who controlled the area between the road and Titova Street?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: The majority of this territory was under the ABH Army control.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please put "ABH," and can you put parallel lines to shade this area from the blue line all the way down there.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And who controlled the part that you didn't shade?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know because I don't know where the Jewish cemetery is here. There is very few things that I can see here in order to be precise in marking.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please put the date and your initials on this picture.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And can we please tender it into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I will allow you just one last question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be tendered into evidence, and then can I have 1D02543. And for the record, I would like to say that this is a shame that this witness could not have been properly examined and that the Defence believe that everything related to this witness should be discarded, because everything was done to the detriment of the Defence case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Unhelpful statement. This was -- it will be admitted as D733. And your last item?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, can we have 1D02543.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this the side of the building viewed from Titova Street that you marked?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you see these two pockmarks on the facade?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are there bullet traces?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I cannot say. Really, I cannot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you circle them in this photograph.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: How do you know this was not caused by shells?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you can see them, what's the point of asking the witness to mark them? It's obvious.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gicevic, if these are rifle bullet traces, where did they come from?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not saying at all that these were rifle bullet traces. This could have been caused by shells as well. And you're asking me about something that I never said. I said that fire came along Marsala Tita Street from the white high-rising building on Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it possible that this could have come from Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So this is viewed from your building and the building of the Hygiene Institute?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I could see this wall from my window.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please put the date and your initials.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Unnecessary. We'll admit this as Exhibit D734.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now it would be necessary to establish whether there was a visibility between this intersection and Grbavica and the distance, but I don't have time for that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you give me a proper picture, I will show to you that there was a line of sight between this place and the white building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just let me consult --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: We have the photograph. We only need time.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: That was said by the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Conclude in 10 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have 1D02544.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is that the same intersection?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, and you can see the tops of the white high-rise buildings on the right and then everything will be clear to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you see the Assembly building?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And where did these incidents happen?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: This is exactly where they happened. I was even present when UNPROFOR fired --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Over the building of the Assembly?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gicevic, do you agree that between this white high-rise building and the incident location, there were enough places where BH Army was deployed?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have this admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D735, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How did it come about that in official documents of the investigators of BH MUP, it is written that you were wounded in the lower leg?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I really don't know the details. I think that you should ask the person who compiled this report. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you have any explanation whatsoever for so many discrepancies and differences in the statements that you gave as well as between your statements and those provided by the police?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know where these discrepancies are. I answered your questions to the best of my knowledge, but the consequences of shelling and bullets are felt both on my body and in my soul.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 1D02534. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gicevic, can you tell us, please, what do you see in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I see the intersection leading to Vrbanja Bridge. I see the Assembly building. I see Zlatiste and the area around the Jewish cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you mark all these locations that you enumerated? What is behind these boards? Is that the old tobacco factory?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is where the old tobacco factory is situated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, can you put an arrow or a number 1 where the old tobacco factory is.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks] This is the old tobacco factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you now mark the Assembly building.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, in the background can you mark these locations on the hill? What is on the very peak of the hill?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Zlatiste [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who controlled Zlatiste, the town and the fortress?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: The Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you see it in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, you cannot, but more or less it is situated here in this forest. I can't see it exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who controlled all these houses in the entire area between the forest and the intersection?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: The line would approximately run like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So in respect of that, where is the Jewish cemetery?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether it's to the left or to the right. I don't know. One centimetre either side. I can't see it clearly [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let me help you, Mr. Gicevic. Is it true that neither to the left, nor to the right, there was no area controlled by the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: It's not correct. They controlled everything to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you draw the separation line?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: This is approximately the separation line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In this photograph, where is the location that you marked back in 1995?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know which place you're referring to, but at any rate, I can't see it in this photograph. If you can provide a more precise resolution or if we move to the right, then I can do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What's the name of the street that leads to Vrbanja Bridge? Is that Vladimir Cosica Street?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: No, I can't remember. It's a very short street and there's only the Assembly building on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Gicevic, could you tell us what number 4 refers to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. It's the street that comes out to the Vrbanja Bridge. It's the place where the UNPROFOR containers were, two of them, there were five or six. And it's impossible that the tram was hit, if this is what Mr. Karadzic insinuates, because there were two or three containers, one on top of the other here, at least five to six metres tall, and the entire intersection was closed off by these containers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you now mark with 5 where the tram stopped after the incident.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: The tram stopped in front of this vehicle or a bit more, about 10 metres or so in this direction [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please write the date and put your initials.

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I believe that the additional time which I was given has been spent now. Can we please have this admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D736, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, do you have any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, but very briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we please have 65 ter 10129 on the screen. And as it is coming up: It is the statement from the 21st of April, 2006, that was discussed during the cross-examination, and I would like to have page 2. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Gicevic, you have spoken during the cross-examination about various statements that you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor in 1995, and here this from 1996. I would like to refer you to paragraph 3. Did you, in fact, make corrections when you gave this statement in 1996, referring to that you made in the previous statement?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, these were the changes about the locations where the tram stopped, because in the English version, when I read it several years later in the Bosnian language, I could see that there was something illogical in the English version of the statement; namely, that I was standing on the left side of the tram.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you also make a correction in relation to whether you used a taxi or not?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I also said that as well, that my memory about that is not clear and that I believed that I walked all the way to the State Hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you. And my last question: You have marked on some maps also today, and I just wanted to confirm with you, when the tram was hit, was that before the bend or curve that you mentioned, in the street, or after?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I assert that the tram was hit before the S-curve, and I know this because, due to fear and because the tram changed the direction quickly, we all fell down, and the tram went on very fast all the way to the place which I marked; that is to say, the old tobacco factory.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. These are my questions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I ask just one question, Your Honours? My learned friend Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff said that a change was made, but it was not changed in 2006, not the location of the incident and the star which marks where the tram was hit. The map has not been corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is that correct, Mr. Gicevic? Item 3 and the entire statement from 2006 do not make any issue about your map from 1995?

utterances.speaker: ALEN GICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know what you are talking about. You have to understand that the victim at the moment when he or she is hit is not looking around and recording and does not have such a power in his head to determine, with half a metre precision, where the incident happened exactly. You have to understand in such panic that one has to see how to save one's head, rather than try to act as a film star, as if the whole incident was filmed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gicevic, you said here that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, it's obvious from his statement. You can make a submission in relation to that. That concludes your evidence, Mr. Gicevic, and I thank you for coming to The Hague to assist the Tribunal. You may leave, and I wish you have a safe journey back home. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was advised that the next witness, who is protected, albeit in a limited nature, needs some time to accommodate the courtroom because he has a face distortion, and I was told that the staff needs some 10 minutes to prepare for him. So we'll have an adjournment for 10 minutes. --- Break taken at 11.46 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: With hindsight, we could have taken a longer break. But we'll have a short break in the middle. Yes. If the witness could take the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated. Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Witness, could you state your full name, please.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: My name is Mirza Sabljica.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: You've previously testified before this Tribunal in the trials of Stanislav Galic, Dragomir Milosevic and Momcilo Perisic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And you've previously given statements to representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, I did give statements to the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: On the 10th and 11th of February of this year, you reviewed an amalgamated statement which consolidated relevant parts of your earlier evidence; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And you had an opportunity to review that statement again when you were here in The Hague about 10 days ago; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: That's also correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Can I have 65 ter 22248, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: On the screen in front of you, do you see the first page of your amalgamated statement?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And would you provide the same answers if you were asked, under oath, about those topics today?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd now seek the admission of the amalgamated statement and the exhibits referred to in the statement, which are listed on the final two pages of the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, we would ask that the amalgamated statement be redacted to exclude two unscheduled incidents, one on page 54, a shelling incident at Kosevsko Brdo on the 8th of November, 1994, and the other on page 63, sniping of a moving car on the 9th of November, 1994. We've dealt with these issues in the past, but we continue to believe that the probative value of including unscheduled incidents is outweighed by the prejudicial effect, particularly the time that would be required and resources for us to have to investigate and present evidence to rebut those incidents. And we also believe that the expenditure of time by the Trial Chamber, given the constraints that it puts on Dr. Karadzic's cross-examination, it would be unwise in admitting these scheduled incidents -- unscheduled incidents. And, finally, it has been our argument that to allow the Prosecution to adduce evidence of unscheduled incidents circumvents Rule 73 bis (D) in which you limited the Prosecution and ordered them to reduce the scheduled incidents in the indictment. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. As Mr. Robinson acknowledges, Your Honours have already ruled on this issue in respect of the amalgamated statement of Ekrem Suljevic, and essentially Mr. Robinson is asking you to address a matter which has been ruled upon. As we submitted in that instance, the unscheduled incidents are relevant to the questions of the widespread and systematic nature of the attack against the civilian population, and they are also relevant to the allegations of a campaign of shelling and sniping. The scheduled incidents are merely illustrative examples of that campaign. And to clarify the record, these incidents were not -- that Mr. Robinson has referred to were not struck from the indictment in accordance with Your Honour's order under Rule 73 bis. They were, in fact, unscheduled to begin with. They were not listed in the schedules in the first place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, the Chamber ruled upon this issue, I just simply reiterate it, although they are not germane to the charges charged in the indictment, but they are relevant to the pattern or the nature of the campaign. So on that basis, we do not accept your request, Mr. Robinson. But let me take a look at the exhibit you referred to. Bear with me a minute. Can I take it you refer to the list of exhibits to be tendered as a part of the associated exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, these are all exhibits which form an integral part of his evidence and which are listed on the last two pages of his statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: My understanding is a lot of items were not up-loaded when the Chamber staff checked with e-court. Are they up-loaded, all the maps and those things? Separate from that, you have no objection to the admission of those exhibits, Mr. Robinson?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President, apart from those that deal with unscheduled incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: We'll double-check that they've all been properly up-loaded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can I raise -- draw your attention to the exhibit, the Rule 65 ter number of which bears the number 20897 --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- which is a CSB investigation file. The report was mentioned during the witness's testimony in a prior case, but the witness was told that he may use that report if he needs to refresh his memory. However, in the amalgamated statement, he never indicated that such an occasion arose, and, therefore, I'm not sure whether it forms a kind of associated exhibit. So, if necessary, I would like you to go through that document. And in the course of the previous witness, there's an investigation report that was deferred to this witness's evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So with that exception -- with the exception of that 20897, all the other items will be admitted. And the numbers of those items will be given in due course by the Court Deputy and circulated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll give the number for his statement now.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P1695, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I now propose to read a summary of the evidence for the benefit of the public. Mr. Mirza Sabljica served as a forensic ballistics analyst with the Security Services Centre, or CSB, in Sarajevo from July 1993. He participated in ballistic investigations of shelling and sniping incidents in Sarajevo. In his statement, he describes the methodology used when investigating incidents, including the method of determining the calibre of the projectile, the direction of fire, and the angle of descent at the point of impact. He also discusses documentary evidence prepared by his team and others relating to a number of different shelling and sniping incidents, including the shelling of a football game in Dobrinja on the 1st of June, 1993, the shelling of a civilian location where a group of children were playing in the snow on 22nd January 1994, the shelling of a residential area in Dobrinja on the 4th of February, 1994, and the shelling of the Markale Market on the 5th of February, 1994. In respect of the Markale Market incident, Mr. Sabljica describes the work done upon his arrival at the scene of the shelling after the shelling had taken place, including the measurement of the shell crater and the inspection of the traces on the ground. He concluded, on the basis of his measurements, that the projectile had come from a north-north-eastern direction at a bearing of approximately 18 degrees. In respect of the shelling of the children playing in the snow on the 22nd of January, 1994, Mr. Sabljica's statement refers to his report of the incident, in which he concluded that the projectiles had been fired from positions in Nedzarici, an area which was under Bosnian Serb control. Mr. Sabljica participated in approximately 60 investigations into incidents of sniping. At least a dozen of those concerned the sniping of trams. In his statement, he describes the methodology of a sniping investigation. Among the sniping incidents he discusses are a sniping attack on the tram of 23rd of November, 1994, and a sniping attack on the tram on the 5th of February, 1994. He states that the origin of sniper fire was often the Metalka building and other high-rise buildings in Grbavica, an area under Bosnian Serb control.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Sabljica, I propose to deal, first of all, with certain sniping incidents, the sniping part of your statement. First of all, this is at pages 60 and 61 of Mr. Sabljica's statement. There's no need for you to refer to it yourself, Mr. Sabljica. In 1996, you said that after the reintegration of Grbavica, you went to visit four high-rise buildings where, on the higher parts of the buildings, you found five or six apartments which had been redesigned to serve as sniper nests. Do you recall that evidence?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And could you briefly describe the nature of the apartments? How did you conclude that they were sniper nests?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Based on the order of the chief of the relevant department and an investigative judge, after the reintegration of Grbavica, we examined certain facilities on the left bank of the Miljacka River from which we suspected fire was opened against civilian buildings and trams during the war in Sarajevo. We made a tour of high-rise buildings in Lenjinova Street, which is now Grbavicka Street. These are four buildings which are 18 floors' tall, each of them, and we managed to locate five or six apartments in these buildings which were redesigned for a specific purpose, to be used as sniper nests, as you call them. I must say that, until then, I had never seen anything like that. But thanks to two of my older colleagues who were then with me - unfortunately, they are no longer alive - Mr. Medjedovic and Mr. Stankov, I managed to get a fuller picture of that. Let me explain how these apartments looked. All the walls in the apartments had been cut in a specific way, or holes had been bored in them so that the outer wall of the apartment, which overlooks the right bank of the Miljacka River, had the smallest opening, and in the next room the opening was bigger, and in the third room it was the biggest opening, where in certain apartments we even found sand sacks and also parapets on which those who were firing against targets on the right bank of the river would lean. So that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd now a request a map which is -- an aerial photograph, in fact, which is 90193.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: When this document comes up, I'd like you to mark the four 18-storey buildings that you just referred to where you found those apartments.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I will mark them now [marks]. It's these four buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you put a "1" next to that, please.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: [Marks] Number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: In your statement, you also refer to - this is pages 62 and 63 - a visit to the Metalka building. Could you mark the Metalka building with a "2," please.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: This is the Metalka building, number 2 [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: In your statement, you say that you did not find the same kind of sniper shelters there that you had seen in the four high-rise buildings. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, I recall that. In Metalka, we did not find something like what we found in the four high-rises in Lenjinova Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: In the Metalka building, did you find anything to suggest that that building had been used as a location for sniper fire -- from which sniper fire could take place?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: One of the apartments, I think, on the eighth floor, because the building has eight floors, we found something that was a sort of improvised snipers' nest with an opening on one of the walls, and we also found some empty shells, automatic weapon empty shells. They were inside the apartment.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you mark on the map the location of the Holiday Inn and place a "3" next to that.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: The Holiday Inn Hotel, here it is [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Are you aware of the location of an S-curve in the tram tracks in that vicinity?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, it's here [indicates]. Should I mark it?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, in your investigation of sniping incidents of trams, specifically, could you give the Court an idea of how many investigations you participated in or with which you are familiar?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Well, we conducted 10 or 12 investigations focusing on trams which were targeted, of which 6 are documented by our findings, because there were victims in these 6, those who were injured or wounded. And it was possible to bring back those cars to the approximate position where they had been hit. And in the other six, it was just a criminal and forensic investigation and there was not sufficient evidence in order to make ballistic reports and analyses, so that we did not even write down such reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you mark on the map the zone in which those sniping incidents took place; the sniping of trams, specifically.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: All along this street, Vojvoda Putnik Street or Smaja od Bosne Street. But let me mark it [marks], but one intersection close to the Social Security building cannot be seen here from Bratstvo-Jedinstvo all the way to Skenderija. This was the dangerous zone, the so-called Sniper Alley, along which it was very risky to move for civilians, vehicles, and anyone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And did all of the tram incidents which you investigated take place within that zone that you've marked?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: All incidents that had to do with trams occurred in the area between the intersection where the Social Security building is to the intersection of Franje Rackog Street and Vojvoda Putnik Street. There, approximately where the S-curve is situated, that was the most dangerous zone for trams. And in the other part of the street, it was more pedestrians, civilians, who were walking along and who were hit.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Can I ask you to mark specifically the beginning and the end of the zone in which the trams were shot at.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you mark the figure 4 at the beginning of the zone and the figure 5 at the end of the zone, please.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, if you could just sign and date that, please. And I would ask that that be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Should I sign the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I would request that that marked up-version of that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. That will be the next Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P1724.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I would now request that 65 ter 07048A be brought up, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could we have the number again?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, no, the exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P1724.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. 1724, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, if we could focus on the top left of the map, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: If you can read that part of the map, could you tell us what that says? If you could just read that out in your own language, Mr. Suljevic -- sorry, Mr. Sabljica.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: "Working Map of the Chief, Command of the 12th dKoV," beginning 0700 hours, 15th of March, 1995, and 700 hours, 31st of May, 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could we now zoom in on central Sarajevo, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Sabljica, are you able to locate the Holiday Inn on this map?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I'll try.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Perhaps we can move the map a little to the right, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If necessary, we can zoom in further.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: If we could move further to the right, please. In fact, we could zoom in a little more, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here [indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: If you could just mark it with an H for the Holiday Inn.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, underneath the Holiday Inn, do you see the pattern of the tram tracks?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you mark the location of the S-curve there, just with S.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Here it is [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Sabljica. If you could sign that. I would ask that that be admitted, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1725, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, you've lived in Sarajevo your whole life; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, I'm a native of Sarajevo and I still live there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: You're familiar with the location of that S-curve from your investigations and from your residency in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Of course. It has not been moved during the last 30 years. I think in the early 1980s the tram tracks were reconstructed and rebuilt, and I think that at that time the S-curve was built there, roughly sometime before the Winter Olympic Games. And since then, it has not been moved.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd now like to show you D654, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: If we could take this map, and this time, Mr. Sabljica, if you could inspect the location of the tram lines in the vicinity of the Holiday Inn. Are you able to see that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Is this map an accurate depiction of the tram lines of Sarajevo during the period 1992 to 1995?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: No. As you can see in this map, the tram tracks go along the Borisa Kidrica Boulevard. I remember that it was the time when the Washington trams were going through Sarajevo, so this map probably dates from the time before the reconstruction, before the Olympic Games, and this tram line did not exist between 1992 and 1995. The tram tracks had already been reconstructed and were looking as they still look today.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Just for clarity, if you could circle the boulevard to which you've just referred.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Is there any indication on this map of an S-curve in front of the Holiday Inn?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Here, at the intersection of Trscanska and Titova. It was also quite a long time ago, before the reconstruction of the tramways in the early 1980s.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I would request you to sign that, please, Mr. Sabljica.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I request that be admitted, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1726, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: For the record, that was the map used by Mr. Karadzic in his cross-examination of Witness Patrick van der Weijden, and the origin of the map is the Government of the United States, Department of Defence of the United States.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to show you two investigation files, Mr. Sabljica. Could I call up 10439, please. The investigation file which is coming up now, Your Honours, deals with incident F16 on the 3rd of March, 1995, which includes the sniping of Alen Gicevic. Do you see the table of contents, as it were, on the right-hand side of the screen in front of you, Mr. Sabljica?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to review this dossier of documents earlier today?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, while I was waiting in the witness room.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could we move to the seventh page in English, which is the fifth page in B/C/S. Could we move to the next page in B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: On the document in front of you, in approximately the middle of the page, it contains your name, Mr. Sabljica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: You were a participant in this sniping investigation; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Are you in a position to confirm that the documents which you inspected relating -- that this dossier of documents is an authentic set of documents?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, it is a whole.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: If we could move to the next page in English and the next page in B/C/S. We may need to enlarge the English somewhat.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: There's a reference here. I'll read it out, Mr. Sabljica. It says: "Members of the Anti-Sniper team of the UNPROFOR French Battalion returned fire. One French soldier was wounded in the head in the exchange of fire." That's the end of the extract. Were you asked to specifically investigate the injury suffered by the French UNPROFOR soldier after the French returned fire?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: On the basis of an order of an investigative judge - I think it was Mr. Mico Potparic, who was head of the team - after we examined the tram in accordance with the instructions issued by the judge, we tried to investigate this wounding incident of the member of the French Battalion. However, his command did not agree, so we did not do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I would request that the -- that this dossier of documents be admitted into evidence, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1727, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I want to take you now, Mr. Sabljica, to another incident. I'd like to call up D681, please. This is an UNPROFOR memorandum dated the 27th of October, 1994, addressed to General Rose. The subject header states: "Sector Sarajevo brief, 26th to 27th October 1994." If we could move to the second page of the document. At the top of the document, Mr. Sabljica, you understand enough English to see the words: "1735 hours, 25 Oct., tram shot area Bratsva Br and reported eight injured"? Do you see that, Mr. Sabljica?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, a few lines further down, we see the words: "All evidence and corroboration by Bosnian officials indicate shots came from Bosnian-held territory." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I want to ask you a couple of questions about that, and I would like to call up 10512A, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: The document in front of you is issued by the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Ministry of the Interior, Security Services Centre, Sarajevo. It's dated the 27th of October, 1994, and it refers, in the first paragraph, to an incident at 1735 hours on the 25th of October, 1994, when a tram came under small-arms fire in the vicinity of the Pofalici tram stop. Mr. Sabljica, you're referred to as the sixth participant in this investigation on this page. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, I do see that. Yes, it is me under number 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: You had an opportunity to review this document earlier today; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: If we could move to the next page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: We see a reference, in the English version, to -- the sentence reads: "In the background of this street runs the Miljacka River, across which in Grbavica PZT there is a three-storey building 120 metres away from the site of the incident. At a certain distance behind it, there is a skyscraper." And if we move to the next page in English, please. We see a reference in the fourth paragraph to the conclusions of the team, and again there's a reference to: "... the direction corresponds to the location of the three-storey building, immediately next to the Miljacka River and the Grbavica PZT." Having reviewed this document earlier today, could you explain what the conclusions of your team were in respect of the origin of fire in this incident?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Of course. As for this tram, since it had moved from the place where it had been hit, the driver was panic-stricken, so he moved the tram. However, in order to carry out a proper investigation, we tried to have the vehicle moved back to approximately the same spot where it had been hit. After our examination, we established that the possible site from which the tram could have been hit was that green building that was on the left bank of the Miljacka in the Street of Obala [indiscernible]. However, from the place where we had placed the tram, we came to the conclusion that there was no optical visibility between the marksman and the tram due to the treetops that acted as an obstacle. At the suggestion of the driver, we established that the tram was supposed to move a few metres ahead, and then in that case, the building would have again been in this suspicious zone. In that case, there would have been visibility and contact from that point of view. At any rate, that bank of the Miljacka River was under VRS control throughout.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Is there anything in this document to suggest that you concluded that the tram had been fired upon by Bosnian Government forces?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Nothing. Nothing gave rise to that suspicion. All indicia showed that this had come from the left bank, that is to say, the area under the control of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd like to move on three pages, please, to a related document. This is dated 2nd of November, 1994, and it's a record of an on-site reconstruction of the incident we've just been looking at and another sniping incident. If we look at the third paragraph, there is a reference to the incident which took place at approximately 1730 hours on the 25th of October, 1994, which concerns tram number 277.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, this document was prepared by you and Mr. Zlatko Medjedovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Towards the end of this document, we see a reference to "the green building." Could you explain what your analysis was with respect to the green building and the incident concerning tram 277?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: That's the building that I talked about a few moments ago. That is to say, this report included the reconstruction of both trams, both 277 and 217. So we had already explained the previous one. We explained that there was no visual contact, as it were, when the tram was put in the original position where it was after -- or, rather, before the reaction of the driver. Aleksandar Vuzina was his name. And then when the tram was moved a few metres, then again it became possible to suspect that that is where the fire had come from that wounded those persons. As for the tram, we established it in a simpler way; on the basis of the traces that were there and seeing the possible site from which it could have come from. It was one of the skyscrapers in Lenjinova Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: The second part of your answer there concerned the second tram; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I mean the second tram. Lest there be any confusion, we dealt with both trams on the same day. This reconstruction took place upon instructions from the judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Can I see the next page in the B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Can you confirm that is your signature at the foot of the page?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, it's my signature and that of the late Zlatko.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And is there anything in this document prepared by you to suggest that fire came from Bosnian Government positions?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Nothing, nothing that would lead to that conclusion that it came from the Bosnian Government positions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just for planning purposes, Mr. Gaynor, how much longer would you need for your redirect -- I'm sorry, your examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Just 25 minutes, I estimate, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That being the case, we will have a short break for 20 minutes now, and then we'll resume at three past 1.00. And then, with the kind indulgence of the interpreters and the other staff, we decided to go until 2.00 this afternoon, if it is agreeable to the parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Very much so. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Twenty minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gaynor, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Before we go on, I'd like to seek the admission of the document the witness was dealing with just before the break. It was 65 ter 10512.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: A?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: A, correct, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit P1728, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like to request document 20897. This was the document Your Honours wished us to put to the witness. I'd like to show the first page, first of all.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, the document in front of you is an investigative dossier of documents relating to an incident which took place on the 27th of February, 1995, at 12.15. And if we could go to the sixth page in B/C/S, which is the tenth page in English, I believe. It might be the 11th page in English. In any event, Mr. Sabljica, do you see your name under number 6 there on that document?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, this document -- according to this document: "At 12.45 on the 27th of February, 1995, the centre was informed by the duty operations officer that fire-arms had been used in Zmaja od Bosne Street and several bullets were fired from enemy territory on the tram en route from the city to Pofalici, and several persons were wounded." Towards -- later on, on the page that you're looking at, there is again a reference to: "The tram was fired on by the aggressor's soldiers ..." Do you recall participating in this investigation, Mr. Sabljica?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: If we could go to page 12 of the English, which is page 9 of the B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: At the top of the page in front of you -- the correct English translation will be coming up. The top of the page in front of you refers to sniper fire from Lenjinova Street in Grbavica, and it says that the bullets were fired from the fourth high-rise building in that street. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to go to a document which you, yourself, authored, and that's on page 22 in English, page 18 in B/C/S, please. If you see the document in front of you now, could you just briefly --

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes. It's the ballistics report which the late Medjedovic and myself drew up.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: While the translation is coming, I'll read out the relevant part of your document. At the end of the document which you signed on behalf of Mr. Medjedovic, Mr. Sabljica, you said: "The possible location from which the bullets had been fired at the tram, garage number 257, could not be determined because it was impossible to return the tram to the exact location where it was hit, as stated by the driver, Sabina Secovic, because the tram broke down as a result of the bullets fired at it." That's at the end of the document, so if we could move one page further on in English and B/C/S. And on the next page in B/C/S, please. Now, first of all, could you confirm that's your signature on that page?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that it is mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: You were signing on behalf of Mr. Medjedovic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you explain to the Court how the conclusion of the investigation, in general, was that fire had come from the high-rise building in Lenjinova Street, whereas the ballistic part of the investigation concluded that it was not possible to determine exactly where fire had come from because the fire could not -- because the tram could not be returned to the exact location? Could you explain your methodology in instances where you couldn't return the tram to the exact location where the fire had taken place?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I just intervene so it would be easier to follow this? These documents are not on the list, so I cannot follow this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: This document is referred to in the amalgamated statement of the witness. This document was.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I need the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't follow. Is this not one of the documents that was offered as an associated exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, this is the exact dossier of documents that Your Honours wished us to put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The 65 ter number of which is 20897?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the latest-to-last, the ERN number I have is 361, so now we have to find our way around. 361 and then onwards, 0331-6361, that's the ERN number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I hope Mr. Sladojevic can sort it out. Yes, let's move on, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: As I was saying, can you explain to the Court what the methodology was in a sniper investigation where you couldn't return the tram to the location where it had reportedly been struck by fire?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: First, to clarify a difference between these two reports, I will stand by what I signed here for Mr. Medjedovic. And why Mr. Kucanin, I believe, and Miokovic signed the report, which says that it was hit from the fourth high-rise, but you have to ask them if you ever call them to testify. And the methods that we used were always one and the same, the methods that we used when we registered damage caused by sniper shots on trams and other vehicles that were moving. We could go back exactly to the spot where the tram was hit -- rather, we couldn't do that, but we made a reconstruction. We could determine the type and kind of damage. We could also see the angles and the direction of movement of the bullets from up, downwards, and from the left to the right. So we did not want to say exactly what was the position from which it was fired, but from the report one could see it was obvious that it had come from the south side. And judging by the side of the tram that was hit, the Grbavica settlement was on that side. And I wouldn't discuss the fourth high-rise building because I never even mentioned it in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you explain the total number of sources of information in a given investigation which might allow a conclusion to be drawn as to the origin of fire?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Once [Realtime transcript read in error "unless"] the on-site investigation team comes at the scene, at the order of an investigative judge, then each member begins to do his work. The ballistics - that's us in this case - with the help of forensic technicians, by using our usual methods, will do our part of the work, and the operative inspectors, such as Mr. Kucanin and Mr. Miokovic, would take the statements of witnesses and use other sources of information from the scene which are available in order to draw up their own report. It happened that certain reports would not be consistent for reasons unknown to me, because the gentleman from the Crime Operations Sector would not wait for the final ballistics report and would draw conclusions on the basis of their own findings and observations. In general, everyone would have to be using one-and-the-same source of information which you can find at the scene of the incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I just want to correct the English transcript, just in case it doesn't get corrected later. The first word the witness said was "Once the on-site investigation team comes," rather than "Unless."

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: In any event, Mr. Sabljica, was your ballistic determination the sole source of information which the whole investigation would have to determine origin of fire?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I don't know about that, but it should have been the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Very well. Let me just put it to you this way: In the file which relates to this incident, and in other files, there were reports given by all of the participants in the investigation; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: The task of a criminal investigation inspector is to list all the names present in the introductory part of his report, which means all the names of team members. However, his report doesn't refer to ballistic aspects and it doesn't contain my name, so this report is signed by him, personally. And as a rule, in order for it to be complete, it should contain a ballistic report as well. In this instance, as you can see, and I can freely say that Mr. Kucanin and the other gentleman reached the conclusions of their own. I don't know on what basis, because such indications were never mentioned in our ballistic report. We even stated the reasons for us not being able to determine that. I don't know why they wrote it as they did and why the investigating judge accepted their report as reliable.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: The dossier contains all the relevant documents in respect of the incident. I'd request that the Trial Chamber admit the entire dossier and afford it the weight that it considers appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Unless it is objected to, we will admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1729, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, I'd now like to move away from sniping to shelling, and I'd like to bring up a video, 65 ter 40125H. Before we start the video:

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: In your statement, Mr. Sabljica, from page 30 onwards, you describe your participation in the shelling of the Markale market-place on the 5th of February, 1994. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Participate in investigation of the shelling?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do. I was a member of the team who carried out the on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Very briefly, could you summarise your role in that investigation?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I was part of the ballistic team, led by the late Cavcic, and Asim Kanlic, the investigating judge, led the entire team. Our task was to determine the direction and the type of the projectile.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd now like to play the first segment, which is 40125H.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you describe, in general terms, what we saw in that portion.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Well, one can see part of the Markale market-place, the stalls, blood-stains, pieces of tissues, scattered fruits, pieces of clothing, some crates or boxes, a lot of blood on the asphalt surface.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we get the date when this video was shot and who shot it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you asking me?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like the Chamber to decide who's going to answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'll leave it to Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. The date of this portion says "5.2.1994." On the screen, itself, the source is AID in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But, Witness, are you aware of that fact; AID took this film on the 5th of February?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know about AID, but I know that, on our team, Zlatan Sadikovic from the CSB was there, and he filmed the scene as well during the investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I should clarify my response earlier. The immediate source of this video to the Office of the Prosecutor was AID. On page 31 of the witness's amalgamated statement, he states -- he's asked the question: "While you were at the scene of the market, did one of the police officers present video-record the market-place?" The answer is: "Yes, that was Mr. Zlatan Sadikovic that did this. He was a member of the investigation team."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd request that that clip be admitted, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: When you tendered all the associated exhibits, was included this one --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- but in your list, it says just one clip, but I take it there are three clips of this?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So you are going to divide it into pieces?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: It might be easiest if Your Honours admit the entire video. It's quite lengthy, so I didn't have time to play that. I was just going to play three portions of it. But it would be our preference to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How long would it be?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'm just getting that information right now. Thirty-four minutes in length.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think I heard that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: It's 34 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thirty-four minutes. But how can we identify this portion from that 34 minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: It has its own 65 ter number, so it could be admitted -- we've previously admitted three extracts from this video with Witness Higgs, Richard Higgs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, and why do we do this? Unless it is objected to, we'll admit this video in its entirety. That would be helpful. It's better for us to have an entire video. And I would ask the Prosecution to identify the proper minutes of each clips you are going to play today.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] However, we are not sure that this was shot on the 5th of January [as interpreted]. One can't see that on this still photo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's a matter for you to cross-examine on.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 5th of February.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could that be done, Mr. Gaynor?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll admit this in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Later on, you can identify --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- the time clips of those videos that are going to be played.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I can actually to it as we go along. The first clip we just played was from 00.20 to 00.58, so that's 20 seconds to 58 seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd like to play the second clip, please, which is from 06.45 to 07.20.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: If we could pause there, please. We're pausing at 7 minutes and 1 second.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, if you could describe what's on the screen in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: You can see an illustration of the method that we used to apply when investigating the origin of fire of the shelling. You align the poles and the central axis, as we used to call it. Because the asphalt was rather wet and full of traces of blood and tissue residue, we were not able to use chalk in order to connect the poles and the center and for drawing up the central axis, so we used these three sticks, depicting the angles and pointing to the direction from which the shell had come.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we get the date of this video?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you have still questions -- it's a subject you need to pursue later on. The witness confirmed that this was filmed the 5th of February, and on that basis we can go on. This is a part of the same video, I take it, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
